task: [.github/workflows/worker-orchestration-tests.yml] 'worker-orchestration-tests' medyan 50 sn (22 kosu). Pip/apt adimlarina actions/cache ekle, gereksiz adimlari paths filtresiyle atla, bagimsiz test adimlarini paralel job'a bol.

evidence.observation: Workflow definition currently executes dependency setup and test suites sequentially without caching layer (`actions/cache` or `setup-python` pip cache) and lacks path filter triggers (`paths` / `paths-ignore`).

factual_findings: Workflow '.github/workflows/worker-orchestration-tests.yml' exhibits a median runtime of ~50 seconds over 22 recorded runs.
Pip and apt dependency installation steps re-download and re-install packages on every run due to missing cache configurations.
Triggers for `push` and `pull_request` lack `paths` filters, causing test runs to execute on unrelated changes (e.g., documentation or unrelated service edits).
Independent test steps are executed sequentially in a single runner job instead of running concurrently in parallel matrix jobs.
hypotheses: Enabling pip caching (`cache: 'pip'` in setup-python or `actions/cache`) will eliminate repeated package downloads and reduce setup time by 15-20 seconds.
Adding `paths` filtering to trigger events will prevent unnecessary workflow executions for non-code and unrelated file commits.
Splitting independent test steps into a parallel matrix or separate jobs will decrease total wall-clock workflow runtime to under 30 seconds.
result.recommendation: Update `.github/workflows/worker-orchestration-tests.yml` to include `cache: 'pip'` under `actions/setup-python`, restrict trigger conditions with `paths` filter for orchestration sources, and refactor test steps into parallel matrix jobs.
result.next_action: Apply the workflow optimizations to `.github/workflows/worker-orchestration-tests.yml`, commit changes, and monitor subsequent execution durations.
